name: NLVR2
ability_definition: The ability to quickly and accurately compare similarities and differences among sets of letters, numbers, objects, pictures, or patterns. The things to be compared may be presented at the same time or one after the other. This ability also includes comparing a presented object with a remembered object.

task_realism.reasoning: Workplace perceptual speed tasks include proofreading, checking numbers against source documents, verifying serial numbers, spotting defects against a reference part, and matching records. NLVR2 asks whether a natural-language statement about object counts, attributes, or relations holds across two web photos. Many items require comparing object sets across the two images, which is loosely related to side-by-side picture comparison. The core demand, though, is language-grounded compositional reasoning, not rapid same/different checking of work-relevant items.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Speed is central to the ability, but there is no time pressure and no latency measurement. Models are fine-tuned on the benchmark's own training distribution and scored offline on a fixed test split. Real work involves high volumes, fatigue-prone repetition, varied inputs, and consequences for missed discrepancies. None of these are present, and the input distribution is narrow curated photo pairs.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only one slice: simultaneous comparison of pictures and objects, measured by accuracy. It omits letters and numbers, patterns, sequential presentation, comparison against a remembered object, and speed. Speed together with accuracy is the defining feature of the ability, so most of the construct is untested.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are real photographs, which is better than toy grids. The output is a binary true/false judgment on a crafted sentence. Real artifacts would be documents, spreadsheets, forms, drawings, or physical items where discrepancies must be flagged or located. The linguistic-query framing is artificial for this ability.

transferability_reasoning: NLVR2 captures a narrow, accuracy-only proxy for simultaneous picture comparison, embedded in a language-reasoning task. It does not test speed, alphanumeric comparison, sequential or memory-based comparison, or realistic work artifacts. High NLVR2 accuracy says little about an AI's ability to rapidly and reliably perform workplace comparison and checking tasks.

2022.metric: accuracy (%) on NLVR2 public test set (test-P)
2022.human_reference: General adult population (typical workers who visually compare pictures or object sets against a description)
